value.rationale: Fingerprinter identified this as a Definitions/Glossary sheet.

Sheet is named 'Core Framework' with PRODUCT FRAMEWORK ID refIds like 'CORE.PRD.001', 'CORE.LOB.001', 'CORE.COV.001' and a Product/LOB/Coverage/Sub-Coverage hierarchy ('Bodily Injury Liability Coverage', 'Pre-Judgment Interest Coverage'), which is the product component model.

The sheet is named 'Core Forms Specifications' with FORM NUMBER values like 'AC 001 AZ', FORM CATEGORY, and FORM EDITION DATE columns, making it a form-presentation catalog rather than attachment rules or rating.

The sheet is titled 'Core Forms Dynamic Data' with FORM NUMBER values like 'AC 107' and FORM NAME 'Waiver of Subrogation Endorsement' alongside DYNAMIC FIELD NAME entries, matching the Dynamic Data / endorsement schedule signature of the forms domain.

The sheet has 'RULE ID' (e.g. 'CORE.RU001'), 'RULE CONDITION', and 'RULE OUTCOME' columns with rule categories like 'Product Eligibility' — the defining signature of a rules sheet, not calculation/algorithm steps.

Despite the sheet name 'Rule References', the stacked tables contain 'TABLE NAME: Minimum Premiums' with an 'Amount ($)' column and class values like 'Truck/Jeep/SUV' and 'Camper Trailer' keyed by state lists, which is an actuarial factor/rate table rather than rule conditions or outcomes.

The sheet named 'Core Rating Specifications' has 'RATING STEP ID' (e.g. 'CORE.RAT.0001.01'), 'ALGORITHM STEP' (e.g. 'Base rate'), 'CALCULATION', and 'RATE REFERENCE' columns defining an ordered rate calculation sequence.
